title: MusicListenBench: Can Audio LLMs Hear the Difference Yet?
abstract: arXiv:2611.29375v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Audio large language models (LLMs) are typically evaluated on song genre, mood, and instrumentation. A more basic skill is telling whether two short clips play the same melody, chord or instrument. We introduce MusicListenBench, a benchmark of paired listening tests for melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo. Each test item comes with two variants. A FLIP variant changes the music, so the answer must change. A STAY variant changes only the sound, such as room echo or hiss, so the answer must stay the same. The two variants have opposite answers, so a model that ignores the audio scores 50%, whatever letter it prefers. The benchmark has a training split and two test sets, one rendered from symbolic music with exact labels and one built from real recordings. translated_title: MusicListenBench：音频大语言模型能听出差异了吗？
translated_abstract: 音频大语言模型（LLM）通常在歌曲流派、情绪和乐器配器等任务上进行评估。而一项更基础的能力是判断两个短音频片段是否演奏相同的旋律、和弦或乐器。我们提出了MusicListenBench，这是一个针对旋律、和声、音色和节奏的成对聆听测试基准。每个测试项包含两个变体：FLIP变体会改变音乐内容，因此正确答案必须改变；STAY变体仅改变声音属性（如房间回声或嘶嘶噪声），因此正确答案必须保持不变。由于两个变体具有相反的答案，任何忽略音频内容的模型无论偏好哪个选项，得分都只能达到50%。该基准包含一个训练集和两个测试集：一个由符号音乐渲染生成并带有精确标签，另一个由真实录音构建。在渲染测试集上，八个开源音频大模型中有七个的得分仅比随机水平高出4分以内。在四个商业模型中，两个GPT-Audio模型均处于随机水平，表现最好的Gemini 2.5 Pro……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出MusicListenBench基准，通过FLIP/STAY成对聆听测试评估音频大模型辨别旋律、和声、音色与节奏的能力，发现绝大多数模型表现接近随机水平，表明现有音频大模型尚不能真正“听出”音乐差异。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MusicListenBench, a paired listening benchmark with FLIP/STAY variants for evaluating audio LLMs on melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo discrimination, finding that most models—including seven of eight open models and both GPT-Audio models—perform near chance level, showing that audio LLMs still cannot reliably hear musical differences.
